**Proposition-level authority:** Stone, Part I-B, joined by Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer: nine votes.

**Limits and questions not reached:** A serious losing claim is not necessarily wholly insubstantial. The panel's merits injunction denial establishes this review channel; no unlocated mailing return is treated as a procedural defect and no universal waiver is presumed.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Goosby v. Osser: applies the narrow wholly-insubstantial exception; a serious losing constitutional claim is not necessarily jurisdictionally frivolous.
- Gonzalez v. Automatic Employees Credit Union and MTM, Inc. v. Baxley: distinguish nonmerits dispositions from this merits denial of injunctive relief.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the three-judge district court's judgment for Georgia and denial of injunctive relief in Nos. 94-631, 94-797 and 94-929, without remand. No injunction or redrawing order is unwound and no new injury inquiry, map order, election cancellation or retained supervision is imposed. The judgment does not certify the entire plan or adjudicate separate claims against federal officials.

### Habeas custody under consecutive sentences

#### [Garlotte v. Fordice](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Garlotte_v_Fordice_merits_1995-05-30.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-6790.
**Decided:** May 30, 1995.

##### Custody under a continuous consecutive series

**Holding:** A prisoner serving a continuous unexpired series of consecutive sentences remains in custody under the earlier conviction when invalidating it would advance release from the aggregate term, although its first segment has been served. This establishes the custody threshold, leaving the conviction’s validity and remaining procedural and merits conditions for review.

**Proposition-level authority:** Ginsburg’s Opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter and Breyer; eight Justices directly support this rule.

**Limits and questions not reached:** An independently expired sentence's collateral consequences alone remain insufficient under Maleng. The rule concerns a continuous unexpired aggregate whose release date would advance; ordinary habeas procedural and merits requirements remain distinct.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Peyton v. Rowe, 391 U.S. 54: extends its aggregate treatment from a future segment to a completed first segment of a still-unexpired consecutive series when invalidation advances release.
- Maleng v. Cook, 490 U.S. 488: distinguishes a wholly expired independent sentence and preserves the rule that collateral consequences alone do not supply custody under that conviction.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reverse the Fifth Circuit's jurisdictional dismissal and remand for remaining procedural and merits review, including review of the district court's merits denial. No conviction is invalidated, writ awarded or immediate release ordered.

### Judicial review of employment-scope certification

#### [Gutierrez de Martinez v. Lamagno](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Gutierrez_de_Martinez_v_Lamagno_merits_1995-06-14.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-167.
**Decided:** June 14, 1995.

##### Review of the scope certification

**Holding:** A Westfall Act scope-of-employment certification is judicially reviewable before substitution of the United States becomes final. Initial substitution on certification does not conclusively establish employment scope; §2679(d)(2) makes certification conclusive for removal only.

**Proposition-level authority:** Ginsburg’s Opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Kennedy and Breyer; six Justices adopt the statutory review rule.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Diversity independently supplies jurisdiction here. Retention under Article III of a nondiverse removed case after rejection of certification, the section 904/headquarters issues outside the grant, actual scope and tort merits remain undecided. No universal discovery entitlement or specified trial mode is required; the foreign-country exception remains effective.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Abbott Laboratories v. Gardner: applies the judicial-review presumption to an ambiguous statutory finality arrangement.
- United States v. Smith: preserves employee exclusivity after scope is established; does not make the certificate conclusive.
- FDIC v. Meyer: preserves the distinction between immunity, actionable claims and employee exclusivity; supplies no certification-finality rule.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reverse and remand for judicial review of employment scope under applicable law with appropriate evidence and procedure, and determination of the proper defendant before immunity and merits. No immunity waiver, tort liability or federal damages action is created.

### Mootness and seasonal permits

#### [Capitol Square Review and Advisory Board v. Pinette](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Pinette_merits_1995-06-29.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-780.
**Decided:** June 29, 1995.

For the other questions in Capitol Square Review and Advisory Board v. Pinette, decided June 29, 1995, No. 94-780. see First Amendment — Private religious displays in public forums (Ohio’s categorical Establishment Clause defense cannot sustain this exclusion).

##### The expired permit dispute remains reviewable

**Holding:** A dispute over a short seasonal permit remains live when its duration prevents full review and there is a reasonable expectation that the same claimant will again face the challenged restriction. These applicants meet both requirements; recurrence affecting other speakers alone would not suffice.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stone, Part I, joined by Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer: nine votes for this threshold holding.

**Limits and questions not reached:** A broader prayer alone does not establish renewed exposure. Reviewability neither revives the expired permit nor extends its relief to every future application.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Weinstein v. Bradford: applies both short duration and same-claimant recurrence; the exception does not extend to every recurring public issue.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the Sixth Circuit at the original scope of the Count One merits judgment: the December 21–24, 1993 permit period remains expired. No new permit, extension, sign condition, removal order, damages or remand is entered. Unappealed rally, damages and other matters remain outside review.

#### [Chabad-Lubavitch of Georgia v. Miller](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Chabad_Lubavitch_v_Miller_merits_1995-06-29.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 93-1047.
**Decided:** June 29, 1995.

For the other questions in Chabad-Lubavitch of Georgia v. Miller, decided June 29, 1995, No. 93-1047. see First Amendment — Private religious displays in public forums (Georgia’s categorical defense cannot sustain summary judgment excluding the private religious display; Interior location does not itself make clearly private expression governmental religion).

##### The recurring access dispute remains live, and only the Rotunda claim is reviewed

**Holding:** A short annual display dispute remains reviewable when full litigation cannot finish within the holiday and the same applicant reasonably expects to seek access again. Chabad’s repeated requests and stated intention to reapply satisfy that rule; this appeal reaches only Count II concerning the Rotunda, not the conceded outdoor-plaza claim.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter, Part I, joined by Stone, Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer: nine votes.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Repeated requests and a stated intention to reapply establish recurrence for Chabad. The conceded outdoor-plaza unattended-object restriction does not apply inside the Rotunda and is not reopened.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Weinstein v. Bradford and Murphy v. Hunt: apply short duration and same-party recurrence; the exception remains claimant-specific.
- Capitol Square Review and Advisory Board v. Pinette: applies the earlier decision’s limited reviewability rule without extending an expired permit.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the Eleventh Circuit reversal of State summary judgment on Count II for further proceedings and lawful relief on neutral terms. No Supreme Court permit, retrospective 1991 display, fixed sign, permanent seasonal entitlement, damages amount or compulsory forum closure is ordered. Count I remains undisturbed; lawful physical, safety, scheduling and identification rules and genuinely prospective viewpoint-neutral forum closure or redefinition remain possible.

### State-tax equitable relief

#### [National Private Truck Council, Inc. v. Oklahoma Tax Commission](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/National_Private_Truck_Council_Inc_v_Oklahoma_Tax_Commission_merits_1995-06-19.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-688.
**Decided:** June 19, 1995.

For the other questions in National Private Truck Council, Inc. v. Oklahoma Tax Commission, decided June 19, 1995, No. 94-688. see Federal Courts — Statutory attorney's fees (Fees follow an available fee-eligible federal claim).

##### Federal tax equity and an actually adequate legal remedy

**Holding:** Section 1983 does not authorize injunctive or declaratory interference with state tax administration where an adequate legal remedy actually protects the claimant. The limitation arises from federal equitable principles informing §1983, not direct application of 28 U.S.C. §1341 to state courts, and does not restrict otherwise lawful state-law equitable relief.

**Proposition-level authority:** Thomas’s Opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; nine Justices adopt this remedial rule.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Extraordinary relief remains possible for irreparable injury, cloud on title or a genuine risk of numerous suits between the same parties involving the same law or facts. Mere parallel claims by many taxpayers do not suffice. An inadequate remedy, including continued unconstitutional taxation after a refund judgment, may change the equitable inquiry. No general exhaustion rule or withdrawal of a promised refund is authorized; the general state-court duty to entertain section 1983 is assumed, not decided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Dennis v. Higgins: preserves the Commerce Clause right; distinguishes right from equitable relief.
- Dows v. Chicago; Matthews v. Rodgers; Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Co. v. Huffman: apply the tax-equity tradition and its adequacy and extraordinary-injury limits.
- Reich v. Collins: preserves an actually honored postpayment remedy; the successful refunds here do not require duplicate equity.
- Harper v. Virginia Department of Taxation: preserves application of governing tax law and meaningful correction, without fixing a single remedy.
- Livadas v. Bradshaw: applies the separation of federal right, enforcement channel and available relief.
- Felder v. Casey; Patsy v. Board of Regents: distinguish hostile state conditions and general exhaustion from this intrinsic federal equitable limitation.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm denial of the reviewed section 1983 injunction/declaration and section 1988 fees while preserving the existing tax invalidity and adequate state-law refund entitlement. No tax sum, separate damages determination, independent state fee ruling or new federal remedial direction follows.

## Holdings volume: maritime-law

# SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES: HOLDINGS REGISTER

**Last completed October Term:** 1994
**Processed through:** June 29, 1995, after all 99 OT1994 inventory Court events and the two admitted source events.
**Edition:** October 1, 2026

## Maritime Law

### Longshore compensation and third-party settlements

#### Estate of Cowart v. Nicklos Drilling Co., 505 U.S. 469 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 91-17.
**Decided:** June 22, 1992.

##### Whether vested compensation entitlement triggers §33(g) before payment or an award

**Holding:** A worker whose substantive compensation right has vested is a person entitled to compensation under LHWCA §33(g), although the employer disputes liability, makes no current payments and is not subject to an award. For a covered third-party settlement below the statutory compensation entitlement, §33(g)(1) requires prescribed written approval from employer and carrier before execution and filing within thirty days; failure to obtain and file the required approval terminates compensation and medical benefits under §33(g)(2). Judgments and settlements at least equal to the compensation entitlement require notification rather than that prior approval.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone, White, Scalia, Souter and Thomas; six Justices adopt vested entitlement, the necessary relationship of approval and notification, and the application. No alternative ground or Marks inquiry supports the ruling.

**Current force:** Remains controlling as stated for vested entitlement and the distinct statutory approval, filing and notification conditions.

**Material application:** Cowart's legal right vested before acknowledgment or adjudication; the informal Labor Department notice was not an award. The estate therefore cannot avoid §33(g) on the theory that the employer was not paying and no award existed. Notification retains an independent role for judgments and sufficiently large settlements.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Not every injured person has a vested compensation right and not every settlement requires prior approval. Employer participation, alternative approval, waiver, gross-versus-net comparison, reopening other final awards, retroactive effect, constitutional challenges and deference to a newly formulated litigation position are undecided. Funding and knowing the settlement are not held incapable of mattering in a properly presented approval or waiver dispute. No new compensation category, equitable exception or general invariant-word canon is created.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the Fifth Circuit on the entitlement question. The administrative award remains overturned; no benefits are restored on the rejected payment-or-award theory, and no new compensation calculation, administrative award or hearing is ordered.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Demarest v. Manspeaker, 498 U.S. 184, requires clear enacted meaning to prevail over contrary administrative practice or retention of isolated words. Chevron U.S.A. Inc. v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc., 467 U.S. 837, and K mart Corp. v. Cartier, Inc., 486 U.S. 281, do not permit deference contrary to unambiguous text; no new litigation-position deference rule is adopted. Sullivan v. Stroop, 496 U.S. 478, and Sorenson v. Secretary of Treasury, 475 U.S. 851, support consistent meaning where linked provisions reinforce it. Banks v. Chicago Grain Trimmers Association, Inc., 390 U.S. 459, supplies approval's protection against inadequate third-party settlement before liability acknowledgment. Northeast Marine Terminal Co. v. Caputo, 432 U.S. 249, and Voris v. Eikel, 346 U.S. 328, retain remedial-construction principles without authorizing a textual exception. Potomac Electric Power Co. v. Director, OWCP, 449 U.S. 268, preserves the Board's adjudicative rather than policymaking role. National Railroad Passenger Corp. v. Boston & Maine Corp., March 25, 1992, preserves Chevron's text-and-structure limits without requiring deference under this different statute. The Board's O'Leary and Dorsey payment-based interpretations are rejected; they are administrative rulings, not Supreme Court precedents.

### Seaman status and compensation

#### Southwest Marine, Inc. v. Gizoni, 502 U.S. 81 (1991)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 90-584.  
**Decided:** December 4, 1991.

##### Whether an LHWCA-listed occupation or voluntary unadjudicated benefits foreclose Jones Act seaman status

**Holding:** Employment in an occupation listed by the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act does not foreclose Jones Act seaman status because the LHWCA expressly excludes a vessel's master or crew. Receipt of voluntary LHWCA benefits without a final adjudication of status does not preclude a Jones Act suit; overlapping recovery remains subject to statutory credit.

**Proposition-level authority:** White's opinion for the Court, joined by Stone, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, and Souter; all eight participants.

**Material application:** The claimed work on floating platforms and during towing leaves genuine disputes about vessel status and employment connection. Listed repair work, lack of propulsion, and absence of living quarters do not resolve those disputes conclusively.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The effect of a final award or settlement, summary judgment on a conclusive record, ultimate crew status, negligence, unseaworthiness, maintenance and cure, and damages remain open.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Ninth Circuit is affirmed, leaving summary judgment reversed for factfinding on status and any viable injury claims. No ultimate status finding or damages award is made; statutory credit applies against overlapping recovery.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** McDermott International v. Wilander supplies the substantial employment-related connection to a vessel in navigation and contribution to its function without requiring traditional navigational duties. Swanson's separation of remedies and Tipton's rule that voluntary compensation does not conclusively determine status are applied unchanged. MCorp's express banking-review preclusion does not create administrative priority in this scheme.

#### [Chandris, Inc. v. Latsis](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Chandris_Inc_v_Latsis_merits_1995-06-14.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-325.
**Decided:** June 14, 1995.

##### Contribution and substantial employment-related vessel connection

**Holding:** Jones Act seaman status requires work contributing to a vessel's function or mission and an employment-related connection to a vessel in navigation or identifiable fleet that is substantial in both duration and nature. The actual assignment governs; a job label or isolated moment aboard is not conclusive, and a genuine change of essential assignment is assessed on the new position rather than mechanically diluted by earlier shoreside service.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's Opinion of the Court, joined at this level by Stone-Zsela, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter and Ginsburg; six support the general connection rule. Stevens, Thomas and Breyer concur only in the judgment on their different actual-crew approach.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Contribution was stipulated but connection remained disputed. Both nature and duration are necessary; later employment may illuminate an earlier relationship but cannot retroactively create status. No job label, isolated voyage or contribution alone conclusively establishes status.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- McDermott International, Inc. v. Wilander, 498 U.S. 337 — applied and clarified: mission contribution is necessary but does not eliminate substantial employment connection.
- Southwest Marine, Inc. v. Gizoni — applied to reject categorical occupational exclusions and preserve genuine connection disputes; conclusive-record summary judgment remains possible.

##### A nonabsolute temporal guide for ordinary assignments

**Holding:** For an ordinary employment arrangement, about 30 percent of service in connection with a vessel in navigation supplies a rule of thumb for substantial duration, not an inflexible cutoff or jurisdictional condition. Justified departures and genuinely changed essential assignments remain possible; courts may resolve status as a matter of law only when the properly assessed facts permit one reasonable conclusion.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's Opinion of the Court, this temporal-guide discussion, joined by Scalia, Kennedy, Souter and Ginsburg; five directly support it. Stone-Zsela does not join this discussion. No judgment-concurrence vote is aggregated into its authority.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Meeting the approximate guide does not establish the independent nature requirement, and falling below it is not invariably dispositive. Competing estimates of Latsis's vessel time are not resolved. Only the five named Justices adopt this temporal guide.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Wilander — clarified through a practical nonabsolute guide to duration; mission contribution remains separately necessary.
- Gizoni — preserved: disputed status ordinarily requires factual resolution, while conclusive-record judgment remains open.

##### The preserved categorical drydock exclusion requires a new trial

**Holding:** Temporary repair does not invariably withdraw a vessel from navigation, although major reconstruction can do so on a sufficient record; withdrawn-vessel time is not automatically qualifying navigation service but may illuminate the actual employment relationship. Here the record did not justify a single categorical navigation conclusion and the instruction excluded the drydock period for every purpose, prejudicing the preserved status issue and requiring a new trial without deciding ultimate status or negligence.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's Opinion of the Court, joined on this preserved instructional holding by Stone-Zsela, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter and Ginsburg; six support this rationale. The three judgment concurrences supply no full-framework join.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Galileo's major rebuilding could support withdrawal from navigation on a conclusive record, but adequate findings or stipulations did not make that instruction unavoidable here. Evidence of withdrawn-vessel work may show assignment continuity without automatically counting as qualifying navigation time. Rules 51 and 61 still require preservation and prejudice.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Senko v. LaCrosse Dredging Corp., 352 U.S. 370 — applied against mechanical repair/immobility exclusions; no finding that every reconstructed vessel remains in navigation follows.
- Butler v. Whiteman, 356 U.S. 271 — applied to genuine navigation/status fact disputes, not to eliminate conclusive-record rulings.
- Wilander and Gizoni — applied to distinguish contribution, connection and factual status from the occurrence of an injury aboard.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the judgment requiring a new status trial with lawful connection instructions and without excluding the entire drydock period for every purpose on this record. Ultimate status, navigation, negligence, causation and damages remain unresolved. The specific preserved drydock objection suffices; broader unpreserved charge objections are not automatically reopened or the charge ratified.

### Maritime settlement credit and contribution

#### [McDermott, Inc. v. AmClyde, 511 U.S. 202](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1993/records/McDermott_Inc_v_AmClyde_merits_1994-04-20.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 92-1479.

**Decided:** 1994-04-20.

##### Proportionate-share credit for maritime settlements

**Holding:** When an injured party settles with some alleged joint tortfeasors in a general maritime action, the claim against the nonsettlers is reduced by the settling tortfeasors’ equitable share of the obligation, not by the settlement dollars. Plaintiff and settlers bear their bargain’s gain or shortfall; the nonsettler owes its adjudicated responsibility and has no contribution claim against the settler for that voluntary settlement shortfall.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s Opinion of the Court, joined by Stone, Blackmun, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg; all nine adopt the rule and its settlement-specific limits.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- United States v. Reliable Transfer Co., 421 U.S. 397 — extended from comparative maritime responsibility to selection of a settlement-credit rule; it had not already decided this issue.
- Edmonds v. Compagnie Generale Transatlantique, 443 U.S. 256 — distinguished as a statutory, nonsettlement allocation case; its joint-and-several liability holding remains binding.

##### Settlement risk, surviving joint liability and this remand

**Holding:** The proportionate-share settlement rule does not generally abolish joint-and-several liability for insolvency or other nonsettlement shortfalls. River Don’s independently found 38 percent share of $2.1 million is $798,000 without a dollar settlement deduction, but the lower court must address the unresolved evidentiary alternative; AmClyde’s unreviewed contractual protection and McDermott’s limitation of its requested recovery remain intact.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s unanimous Opinion of the Court; all nine adopt this application and the bounded reversal and remand.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Edmonds v. Compagnie Generale Transatlantique, 443 U.S. 256 — preserved: voluntary settlement risk does not resolve unrelated joint-liability shortfalls.
- United States v. Reliable Transfer Co., 421 U.S. 397 — applied to the independently found responsibility share without supplying an unmade allocation within the combined 30 percent.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The settlement price is not a fault finding, and it does not divide the combined 30 percent allocation to McDermott and the sling defendants. Reliable allocation and an opportunity to present evidence remain necessary where material. Ordinary settlement-validity challenges and nonsettlement shortfalls remain distinct.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Fifth Circuit's dollar-credit ruling as to River Don is reversed and the case remanded. Its 38 percent of $2.1 million is $798,000 before any resolution of the unpassed evidentiary alternative; payment is not ordered unconditionally. AmClyde's contractual protection, the settlement and the limit on recovery requested remain intact.

#### [Boca Grande Club, Inc. v. Florida Power & Light Co., 511 U.S. 222](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1993/records/Boca_Grande_Club_v_Florida_Power_Light_merits_1994-04-20.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 93-180.

**Decided:** 1994-04-20.

##### Proportionate-share credit supplies the protection that makes contribution against the settler unavailable

**Holding:** In a general maritime tort action governed by proportionate-share settlement credit, the plaintiff’s claim against nonsettlers is reduced by the settling tortfeasor’s equitable share, and a nonsettler may not recover contribution from the settler merely because the settlement price is less than that share. The lower court must permit meaningful litigation and reliable determination of comparative responsibility; it may not withhold equitable-share protection while invoking settlement finality to bar contribution.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s opinion for the Court, joined in full by Stone-Zsela, Blackmun, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg; nine Justices adopt this application of McDermott.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- McDermott, Inc. v. AmClyde, decided earlier April 20, 1994: applied; proportionate-share reduction supplies the basis for denying contribution against a settler for a settlement-price shortfall.
- United States v. Reliable Transfer Co., 421 U.S. 397 (1975): preserved as the comparative-fault foundation requiring reliable allocation.
- Edmonds v. Compagnie Generale Transatlantique, 443 U.S. 256 (1979): distinguished; its statutory nonsettlement setting does not control this bargain or abolish the settlement-credit rule.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The rule supplies proportionate-share protection rather than freestanding immunity for every settler. Independent contractual indemnity, fraud or invalidity, unrelated joint-liability shortfalls, exoneration and limitation remain unadjudicated.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Eleventh Circuit judgment is vacated and remanded for application of McDermott and reliable allocation. No percentage, damages award, exoneration or limitation judgment is entered; Boca Grande's unpassed alternative factual objection is not independently decided.

### State maritime forums

#### [American Dredging Co. v. Miller, 510 U.S. 443](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1993/records/American_Dredging_Co_v_Miller_merits_1994-02-23.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 91-1950.

**Decided:** 1994-02-23.

##### State forum administration under the saving clause and Jones Act

**Holding:** A competent state court hearing this domestic Jones Act and accompanying in personam maritime action need not employ the federal doctrine permitting dismissal in favor of a more convenient forum; Louisiana may retain the action under Article 123(C). That choice changes neither federal maritime liability and remedies nor jurisdiction, and it decides no independent discrimination, Commerce Clause, or foreign-party question.

**Proposition-level authority:** The statutory/state-forum portion of Scalia's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, and Ginsburg; seven Justices adopt this sufficient ground for affirmance. Stevens joins this portion and the judgment, but not the separate Jensen analysis.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Missouri ex rel. Southern Railway Co. v. Mayfield, 340 U.S. 1: its state-forum choice for FELA actions carries through the Jones Act; its requirement of impartial local policy, without discrimination against federal claims or sister-state citizens, remains intact. A residence distinction that treats all nonresidents alike is not equated with citizenship discrimination.
- Bainbridge v. Merchants & Miners Transportation Co., 287 U.S. 278: applied to preserve state-court Jones Act venue rules; venue and discretionary dismissal remain distinct.

**Independent alternative holding:** Louisiana's refusal to dismiss this domestic in personam maritime action for convenience neither materially prejudices a characteristic feature of general maritime law nor interferes with its proper harmony and uniformity. Forum non conveniens governs forum administration rather than primary maritime obligations; a procedural label alone, however, does not protect a state rule that impairs a substantive maritime right or an integral burden or remedy.

**Proposition-level authority for alternative holding:** The Jensen portion of Scalia's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, Blackmun, O'Connor, Souter, and Ginsburg; six Justices adopt this independently sufficient ground. Stevens does not join it. Souter also supplies a separate close-classification qualification without withdrawing this join.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Southern Pacific Co. v. Jensen, 244 U.S. 205: applied and left in force; neither characteristic-feature protection nor necessary maritime uniformity requires the dismissal procedure here.
- Gulf Oil Corp. v. Gilbert, 330 U.S. 501, and Piper Aircraft Co. v. Reyno, 454 U.S. 235: their federal convenience inquiry remains applicable in the courts governed by it, including the adequate-alternative-forum prerequisite, relevant private/public considerations, appropriate weight to forum choice, and abuse-of-discretion review; it is not imposed on this state court.
- Miles v. Apex Marine Corp., 498 U.S. 19: its statute-bounded uniformity of substantive maritime recovery is preserved, not converted into a uniform forum-management command.
- Sun Oil Co. v. Wortman, 486 U.S. 717: its context-sensitive substance/procedure distinction supports attention to legal function; it supplies no categorical maritime exemption for procedural labels.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The holding concerns a competent state court and domestic in personam claims. Maritime liability, remedies, integral burdens, independent discrimination and Commerce Clause objections, and foreign-party controversies are not resolved by treating forum administration as procedural. Jensen remains in force.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Louisiana Supreme Court is affirmed, preserving its reversal of the convenience dismissal and remand. The injury claims may proceed in state court. No interstate transfer, federal convenience reweighing or liability award is ordered; the unpursued personal-jurisdiction objection is not decided.

### Vessel turnover warnings

#### [Howlett v. Birkdale Shipping Co., S.A., 512 U.S. 92](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1993/records/Howlett_v_Birkdale_Shipping_Co_SA_merits_1994-06-13.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 93-670.

**Decided:** 1994-06-13.

##### The cargo turnover-warning duty is limited by the vessel’s assigned care

**Holding:** A vessel must warn an unloading stevedore of a hazard the vessel knows or should know through its required reasonable care, likely to be encountered in the work and neither known nor obvious to, nor reasonably anticipated by, a competent stevedore. For a cargo-stow hazard, that duty does not ordinarily require supervising independent loading operations or inspecting their completed work; an established contract, positive law or custom may alter that allocation, but none is established here.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's unanimous Opinion of the Court; Stone-Zsela, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg adopt the limited turnover-warning rule and rejection of a general cargo-inspection duty.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court does not establish a contract, positive-law or customary enlargement of the vessel's duties. Section 905(b)'s bar on direct or indirect employer liability to the vessel for these damages and contrary agreements remains; no indemnity or seaworthiness claim is revived.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Scindia Steam Navigation Co. v. De Los Santos, 451 U.S. 156: applies the allocation of cargo responsibility and specifies its limited turnover warning duty; the separate active-control and intervention duties remain intact.
- Federal Marine Terminals, Inc. v. Burnside Shipping Co., 394 U.S. 404: preserves ordinary care within the vessel's legally assigned responsibilities, without a universal contractor-inspection rule.

##### Knowledge and obviousness require the correct actor and time on remand

**Holding:** The turnover-warning claim must be reconsidered because possible crew knowledge during loading and a hazard's visibility to a competent unloading stevedore are distinct inquiries. Supplying plastic alone does not prove knowledge of its dangerous placement, and loading-stage visibility does not itself establish unloading-stage obviousness; the full record may still support summary judgment, and no negligence, latent hazard, causation or damages is found here.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's unanimous Opinion of the Court; Stone-Zsela, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg adopt this application and bounded vacatur and remand.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court does not attribute knowledge to the vessel merely because somebody aboard might have seen material. Actual crew role, awareness and unloading visibility remain questions for proper summary-judgment assessment; renewed summary judgment remains possible.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Scindia Steam Navigation Co. v. De Los Santos, 451 U.S. 156: applies the distinct vessel-knowledge and competent-stevedore warning conditions to the actual turnover setting; neither condition is presumed from the accident.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Third Circuit's judgment is vacated and the turnover-warning claim remanded for reconsideration on the full summary-judgment record. The lower courts must distinguish vessel knowledge from conditions confronting a competent unloading stevedore and address contrary visibility evidence. Renewed summary judgment remains possible; no trial, negligence, causation or compensation is ordered.

### Vessel-caused land injury and mixed maritime activity

#### [Jerome B. Grubart, Inc. v. Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Co. / City of Chicago v. Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Co.](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Jerome_B_Grubart_Inc_v_Great_Lakes_Dredge_Dock_Co_merits_1995-02-22.md)

**Docket or dockets:** Nos. 93-762; 93-1094.
**Decided:** February 22, 1995.

##### Vessel-caused land injury satisfies admiralty locality through ordinary proximate causation

**Holding:** Under 28 U.S.C. §1333(1) and the Admiralty Extension Act, damage consummated on land satisfies admiralty's location requirement when it is proximately caused by a vessel on navigable waters. The alleged damage caused by barge-based piling equipment to the underwater tunnel meets that requirement at this jurisdictional stage; neither a fixed distance nor a fixed interval between the vessel operation and land flooding replaces the ordinary causal inquiry.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter's opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Kennedy and Ginsburg: five of seven participating Justices, a direct majority. Scalia and Thomas concur in the judgments only.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Gutierrez v. Waterman Steamship Corp., 373 U.S. 206, supplies the Extension Act's reach to vessel-caused land harm. Executive Jet Aviation v. Cleveland, 409 U.S. 249, and Sisson v. Ruby, 497 U.S. 358, preserve a separate maritime-connection inquiry; satisfying locality alone does not displace that inquiry in the Court's framework.

##### This underwater-structure incident and vessel-based repair activity satisfy Sisson

**Holding:** The maritime-connection requirement examines the potential effect on maritime commerce of the general type of incident and the substantial relationship between the activity giving rise to it and traditional maritime activity. Damage by a vessel on navigable water to an underwater structure has the required potential, and repair or maintenance of waterway structures performed from a vessel has the required relationship; the actual closure of navigation corroborates this application but is not a universal prerequisite.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter's opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Kennedy and Ginsburg: five of seven participating Justices, a direct majority. Scalia and Thomas concur in the judgments only.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Sisson v. Ruby, 497 U.S. 358, is applied to general incident characterization and substantial maritime activity. Foremost Insurance Co. v. Richardson, 457 U.S. 668, preserves admiralty's concern beyond collisions between commercial vessels. Executive Jet's rejection of locality alone remains part of the Court's framework; the separate writings' simpler rule does not replace it.

##### An alleged maritime proximate cause is not erased by a contributing nonmaritime actor

**Holding:** For the activity branch of Sisson, the substantial maritime relationship is satisfied when at least one alleged tortfeasor's relevant maritime activity is an alleged proximate cause of the incident; a contributing actor's nonmaritime conduct does not erase that connection. This rule establishes jurisdiction over the connected maritime claim, not automatic jurisdiction over every joined party or independent claim, and it decides neither liability nor entitlement to statutory limitation.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter's opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Kennedy and Ginsburg: five of seven participating Justices, a direct majority. Scalia and Thomas concur in the judgments only.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Sisson's express mixed-activity reservation is resolved only for the causally connected incident described here. American Dredging Co. v. Miller, February 23, 1994, preserves saving-to-suitors and competent-state-forum distinctions without altering admiralty jurisdiction. McDermott, Inc. v. AmClyde and Boca Grande Club v. Florida Power & Light, April 20, 1994, retain their defined settlement/contribution rules, not a general jurisdictional or limitation entitlement.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Seventh Circuit is affirmed in both dockets, 7–0. The limitation proceeding may continue within the recognized admiralty jurisdiction; liability, statutory limitation, privity, corporate knowledge and personal-contract merits are not decided. The lower reversal of the alternative pleading dismissal remains intact, and independent claims retain ordinary jurisdictional requirements.

### Cargo arbitration and nonwaivable carrier obligations

#### [Vimar Seguros y Reaseguros, S.A. v. M/V Sky Reefer](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/Vimar_Seguros_y_Reaseguros_SA_v_MV_Sky_Reefer_merits_1995-06-19.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-623.
**Decided:** June 19, 1995.

##### Foreign arbitration costs and COGSA nonwaiver

**Holding:** COGSA §3(8) does not invalidate the Tokyo arbitration clause merely because the selected forum increases inconvenience or enforcement expense. The FAA does not override nonwaivable COGSA substantive protection; the statutes operate together while that protection remains available.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy’s Opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, O’Connor, Scalia, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg; seven participating Justices adopt this statutory coexistence ground.

**Limits and questions not reached:** True foreign-court clauses, practical foreclosure on a materially different record and demonstrated substantive waiver remain open. Indussa's increased-cost inference is rejected for this arbitration clause, while its foreign-court application is reserved. The excluded adhesion defense is not reopened. COGSA's duties and notice/suit periods retain their protection despite ordinary forum expense.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Mitsubishi Motors Corp. v. Soler Chrysler-Plymouth, Inc.: applies forum/substantive-right distinction and preserves its prospective-waiver reservation.
- Allied-Bruce Terminix Cos. v. Dobson; Mastrobuono v. Shearson Lehman Hutton; First Options of Chicago v. Kaplan: preserve actual FAA coverage, consent, choice-of-law and review limits, without overriding COGSA.

##### Retained jurisdiction and a concrete statutory-waiver objection

**Holding:** The present record does not establish that arbitration will diminish nonwaivable COGSA protection. The district court must retain the action during arbitration; the stay neither authorizes prospective waiver nor forecloses a properly supported statutory objection through the remedial authority lawfully available at enforcement.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy’s Opinion of the Court; the same seven Justices support the retained-jurisdiction rule and remand.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No actual foreign-law rule, stowage-defense validity or diminished carrier liability is found. A demonstrated unambiguous tandem waiver with no lawful later protection cannot be cured merely by postponing review. The present speculative reduction does not establish that premise; final cargo liability and nondelegable duty remain undecided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Mitsubishi Motors: preserves a concrete prospective-waiver/public-policy objection while distinguishing the presently speculative reduction.
- First Options: retains the actual bounds on judicial review and agreement; does not guarantee unlimited review of arbitral merits.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the First Circuit arbitration stay and remand with the domestic action retained during arbitration. A concrete statutory-waiver objection remains available through properly invoked enforcement authority. No action dismissal, agreement rewriting, cargo-liability decision, hypothetical award review or plenary arbitral-merits review is ordered or guaranteed.

### Prejudgment interest and comparative fault

#### [City of Milwaukee v. Cement Division, National Gypsum Co.](https://github.com/Alex-Oss222/scotus-career/blob/main/terms/OT1994/records/City_of_Milwaukee_v_Cement_Division_National_Gypsum_Co_merits_1995-06-12.md)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-788.
**Decided:** June 12, 1995.

##### Mutual fault and ordinary liability uncertainty do not defeat maritime interest

**Holding:** Maritime prejudgment interest ordinarily compensates loss of use of an otherwise compensable amount; departure requires a legally sufficient exceptional circumstance supported by the record. Mutual fault already reflected in principal damages and a genuine ordinary liability dispute, without more, do not justify denial; undue claimant-caused delay can qualify, but the Court adopts no exhaustive list, fixed liquidated-claim prerequisite, rate, period, compounding rule or sum.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg; all eight participating Justices adopt the complete rule and affirm the calculation remand.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No nonmaritime interest statute is transplanted. Municipal status, sovereign immunity and a categorical municipal-financing exception are not adjudicated; the municipal-status alternative was not pursued.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** The Scotland, 118 U.S. 507, is applied to compensatory equitable discretion, not unbounded fairness. United States v. Reliable Transfer Co., 421 U.S. 397, is applied to proportional collision fault and the avoidance of a second deduction for that same fault. McDermott and Boca Grande retain their separate maritime settlement/contribution rules; neither creates an interest exception.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the calculation remand without disturbing the settled $1,677,541.86 principal paid in January 1992 or the two-thirds National Gypsum/one-third City fault allocation. The requested $5,317,807.70 is not an award. Rate, period, compounding, quantum and lawfully open distinct exceptional circumstances require determination.

## Holdings volume: criminal-procedure

# SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES: HOLDINGS REGISTER

**Last completed October Term:** 1994
**Processed through:** June 29, 1995, after all 99 OT1994 inventory Court events and the two admitted source events.
**Edition:** October 1, 2026

## Criminal Procedure

### Appellate finality

#### United States v. Ibarra, 502 U.S. 1 (1991)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 90-1713.  
**Decided:** October 15, 1991.

##### Whether a timely reconsideration motion renewing an abandoned suppression ground postpones appellate finality

**Holding:** A single timely motion asking a district court to alter a suppression ruling renders that ruling nonfinal for appeal purposes until the motion is decided, even when the motion renews a ground the Government earlier abandoned. The full appeal period begins upon disposition of the motion; the rule does not decide whether the renewed ground remains waived on the merits.

**Proposition-level authority:** Per curiam opinion joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, and Souter; unanimous eight-Justice participating Court.

**Material application:** The Government's January 30 notice of appeal was filed within thirty days after the January 3 denial of reconsideration.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Bad-faith and successive motions, the substantive effect of abandonment, and the Fourth Amendment validity of the search are unresolved. Existing appeal periods and preservation rules are unchanged.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Tenth Circuit's dismissal of the appeal is vacated, and the case is remanded for further appellate proceedings.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** United States v. Healy supplies suspension of finality on a timely criminal rehearing request. United States v. Dieter forecloses an exception based on the kind or strength of the asserted error. Department of Banking v. Pink is distinguished because its filing sought no substantive alteration of adjudicated rights.

### Capital sentencing

#### Sochor v. Florida, 504 U.S. 527 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 91-5843.
**Decided:** June 8, 1992.

For the preservation bar on the jury-heinousness instruction claim in *Sochor v. Florida*, June 8, 1992, No. 91-5843, see Federal Courts — Adequate and independent state grounds.

##### Whether the judge's conscious-victim strangulation application supplies a sufficiently narrowed heinousness aggravator

**Holding:** A sentencing judge may apply an otherwise vague heinousness aggravator through an authoritative and sufficiently specific state narrowing construction. Florida's consistently recognized conscious-victim strangulation construction supplies adequate guidance here; inconsistent applications in other factual settings do not establish that this judge lacked guidance.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part II-B of Souter's opinion, joined by Stone, White, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas; seven Justices. Blackmun and Stevens do not join this disposition because they would require correction of the separate jury defect.

**Current force:** Remains controlling at the stated judicial application and record.

**Material application:** Florida's identified narrowing decisions address the fear and conscious suffering of strangulation. The victim's resistance, fear and strangulation support that concrete construction; the judge did not merely repeat the statutory adjectives.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court approves neither every Florida heinousness decision nor the bare instruction given to this jury, and it does not decide a different victim's condition.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reject the preserved constitutional challenge to the judge's narrowed heinousness application; that factor supplies no basis for relief.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Godfrey v. Georgia*, 446 U.S. 420, and *Maynard v. Cartwright*, 486 U.S. 356, require meaningful narrowing. *Walton v. Arizona*, 497 U.S. 639, permits reliance on authoritative state constructions and presumes the judge's familiarity with them. *Proffitt v. Florida*, 428 U.S. 242, preserves a narrowed heinousness category without approving every later application.

##### Whether submission of a lawful but unsupported coldness aggravator establishes that a general advisory jury recommendation relied on it

**Holding:** Submitting a legally available aggravating circumstance without evidentiary support does not itself establish that a Florida advisory jury relied on it in a general death recommendation that identifies no aggravator findings. The asserted inference of jury-coldness error is rejected without a finding that the jury actually rejected the factor or resolution of a legally invalid instruction.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part III-A of Souter's opinion, joined by White, O'Connor, Kennedy and Thomas; five Justices. Stone reserves this independent question, Blackmun and Stevens would include the submission in correction, and Scalia does not join this holding.

**Current force:** Remains controlling at this narrow factual-insufficiency inference and general advisory recommendation.

**Material application:** Cold, calculated and premeditated murder was a lawful aggravator, but proof of its heightened premeditation requirement failed. The jury identified no aggravator findings, so submission alone cannot establish its reliance. The judge's express coldness finding establishes a separate error.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The holding makes no factual jury finding, does not assimilate every capital recommendation to a guilt verdict, does not decide that all instructional errors are harmless, and leaves broader capital-jury doctrine open. Legally invalid alternatives remain distinct.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Griffin v. United States*, December 3, 1991, is extended narrowly through its factual-versus-legal distinction to this asserted inference from a general advisory recommendation. *Stromberg v. California*, 283 U.S. 359, and *Yates v. United States*, 354 U.S. 298, retain their rules for legally invalid alternatives. *Estelle v. McGuire*, December 4, 1991, retains whole-charge reasonable-likelihood review, which neither removes the preservation bar nor supplies an automatic inference of factual reliance here.

##### Whether the judge's express weighing of the evidentially unsupported coldness aggravator creates constitutional error

**Holding:** When a Florida capital sentencing judge expressly weighs an aggravator that the state supreme court holds unsupported by the evidence, that invalid factor creates Eighth Amendment error in the weighing decision. Lawful reweighing, constitutional harmless-error review or resentencing is required; other valid aggravators do not themselves cure the error.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part III-B-1 of Souter's opinion, joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy and Thomas; eight Justices. Scalia rejects the constitutional weighing-error premise.

**Current force:** Remains controlling as stated for documented reliance on an unsupported aggravator.

**Material application:** The judge expressly found and weighed heightened coldness, which Florida held unproved. Proof of ordinary murder premeditation does not establish this additional aggravating requirement. Surviving death eligibility therefore does not eliminate the actual weighing error.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The convictions and mitigation findings are not disturbed. Removal of an aggravator does not itself require a life sentence or a new penalty jury. The no-mitigation finding does not mean no mitigating evidence was presented.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The sentence requires a supported determination under *Chapman*, lawful reweighing if Florida law authorizes it, or resentencing. The separate holding below identifies why the existing appellate treatment fails to provide that correction.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Clemons v. Mississippi*, 494 U.S. 738, requires adequate correction of capital weighing error. *Parker v. Dugger*, 498 U.S. 308, applies that principle to unsupported Florida aggravators and the actual sentencing record. *Stringer v. Black*, March 9, 1992, supplies the correction principle for this documented reliance; its habeas retroactivity and default reservations do not bar direct review. *Zant v. Stephens*, 462 U.S. 862, is distinguished because its nonweighing setting does not make surviving eligibility an automatic cure. *Chapman v. California*, 386 U.S. 18, supplies constitutional harmlessness with the State bearing the burden.

##### Whether Florida's proportionality discussion and surviving-factor count constitutionally cure the weighing error

**Holding:** A state appellate court affirming this sentence must substantively establish beyond a reasonable doubt that the invalid aggravator did not contribute to the sentence, or provide another authorized constitutional cure. Florida's existing proportionality discussion, count of surviving factors and mixed citations do not establish that inquiry; no verbal formula is either required or sufficient.

**Proposition-level authority:** Parts III-B-2 and IV of Souter's opinion, joined by Stone, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor and Kennedy; six Justices. White and Thomas accept the error framework but find the existing review sufficient; Scalia would affirm on a separate ground.

**Material application:** Proportionality compares sentences across cases; it does not itself determine whether this invalid factor influenced this sentencing balance. Three valid factors and no found mitigation may bear on harmlessness but do not establish the missing inquiry. The State bears the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt burden.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court neither undertakes reweighing nor determines the outcome of lawful correction. It requires no prescribed phrase and rejects a bare harmless-error label as sufficient. No automatic life sentence, mandatory new penalty jury, new mitigation finding or new habeas standard is created.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Vacate the judgment sustaining the death sentence and remand to Florida for supported *Chapman* review, lawful reweighing if Florida law permits, or resentencing. The convictions remain intact; the state courts must choose and perform an adequate lawful correction.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Chapman v. California*, 386 U.S. 18, retains the State's burden to establish beyond a reasonable doubt that the error did not contribute. *Clemons v. Mississippi*, 494 U.S. 738, and *Parker v. Dugger*, 498 U.S. 308, require corrective analysis of the sentence and actual record rather than proportionality alone. *Stringer v. Black*, March 9, 1992, preserves the inadequacy of factor counting and proportionality as standalone cures.

#### Morgan v. Illinois, 504 U.S. 719 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 91-5118.
**Decided:** June 15, 1992.

##### Whether an automatic-death juror is disqualified from a capital sentencing jury

**Holding:** When a State provides a jury to decide a capital sentence, due process requires an impartial jury. A juror who would automatically impose death upon conviction regardless of the facts and required consideration of mitigation is subject to challenge for cause; if such a juror serves and death is imposed, that sentence cannot be executed.

**Proposition-level authority:** White's opinion of the Court, joined by Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy and Souter; six Justices adopt this proposition. Stone concurs in the judgment without a formal opinion join; Scalia and Thomas dissent.

**Material application:** Illinois requires consideration of aggravation and mitigation. A juror who fixes death in advance regardless of the evidence refuses that task; the conclusion a qualified juror reaches after genuine consideration is different.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The State need not provide jury sentencing, but a jury it supplies must be impartial. General support for capital punishment is not disqualifying, and the Court prescribes no weight for mitigation or required punishment. Witt's substantial-impairment standard remains intact.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The death-sentence affirmance is reversed and remanded, 7–2. The conviction is undisturbed; no automatic life sentence or constitutional right to jury sentencing is imposed.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Wainwright v. Witt, 469 U.S. 412 (1985), and Adams v. Texas, 448 U.S. 38 (1980): applied to views disabling lawful performance; their governing substantial-impairment rule is not replaced.
- Witherspoon v. Illinois, 391 U.S. 510 (1968): its impartiality principle applies to the opposite categorical disability; ordinary death-penalty views remain permissible.
- Ross v. Oklahoma, 487 U.S. 81 (1988): its automatic-death-juror principle is expressly adopted; its result rested on removal of the identified juror.
- Lockett v. Ohio, 438 U.S. 586 (1978), and the received mitigation line: retained as requiring a real opportunity for individualized consideration, not a prescribed result.

##### Whether requested inquiry must expose automatic-death views despite general assurances of fairness and obedience

**Holding:** On a capital defendant’s request, voir dire must adequately inquire into whether prospective sentencing jurors would automatically impose death regardless of lawful consideration of the facts and mitigation. General promises of fairness and obedience to instructions did not cover that subject here; the denied inquiry requires reversal of the death-sentence affirmance and remand, without disturbing the conviction.

**Proposition-level authority:** White's opinion of the Court, joined by Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy and Souter; six Justices adopt this proposition. Stone concurs in the judgment without a formal opinion join; Scalia and Thomas dissent.

**Material application:** Generic assurances can conceal a prospective juror's belief that automatic death is fair. One juror's volunteered disqualifying answer and removal do not show adequate subject coverage for the others. The defendant need not prove answers to an inquiry he was forbidden to make.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No actual bias is found in a seated juror. Trial judges retain control over wording and follow-up, and no fixed questionnaire or new proof quantum is required. Unrelated voir dire omissions, collateral review and retroactivity remain undecided.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The death sentence is set aside for lawful further sentencing proceedings without this defect. If Illinois uses a future capital jury, selection must comply with the inquiry rule; the Court does not require jury sentencing, order a guilt retrial or impose life imprisonment.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Wainwright v. Witt, 469 U.S. 412 (1985): its requirement of demonstrating bias through questioning supports the necessary opportunity to inquire.
- Mu’Min v. Virginia, 500 U.S. 415 (1991): distinguished; discretion over the detail of an inquiry does not authorize complete omission of this necessary subject.
- Lockhart v. McCree, 476 U.S. 162 (1986): its recognition of the opportunity to identify disqualified jurors is applied to the defendant’s corresponding challenge.
- Turner v. Murray, 476 U.S. 28 (1986): its protection against unacceptable capital-sentencing risk supports required subject coverage and sentence-only relief.

#### Espinosa v. Florida, 505 U.S. 1079 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 91-7390.
**Decided:** June 29, 1992.

##### A legally influential recommendation cannot rest on an inadequately narrowed aggravator

**Holding:** When a weighing State requires its sentencing judge to give great weight to a jury's recommendation, an inadequately narrowed aggravating instruction to that jury can infect the final sentence even if the judge directly finds only valid aggravators. The especially wicked, evil, atrocious or cruel instruction given here lacks the guidance the Eighth Amendment requires; the judge's separate findings do not by themselves cure the recommendation's legal influence.

**Proposition-level authority:** The per curiam opinion, joined by Stone, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter and Thomas; seven Justices adopt the defect and corrective requirements. White favors argument and casts no present merits vote; Scalia dissents.

**Material application:** The jury returned an 11–1 general death recommendation under the unelaborated instruction. The judge gave operative weight to four aggravators and found two mitigators. No factor-specific jury finding is inferred; the required legal weight of the recommendation supplies the indirect channel of error.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Godfrey v. Georgia, 446 U.S. 420 (1980), Maynard v. Cartwright, 486 U.S. 356 (1988), and Shell v. Mississippi, 498 U.S. 1 (1990): apply their requirement of meaningful guidance for a capital aggravating category; the instruction here is insufficiently narrowed.
- Stringer v. Black, simulated March 9, 1992: applies the distinction between valid eligibility and constitutionally defective weighing; surviving valid aggravators alone do not remove the error.
- Sochor v. Florida, simulated June 8, 1992: applies its weighing-error rule while distinguishing its independent state preservation bar to a different jury claim and its separate factual-invalidity issue.
- Mills v. Maryland, 486 U.S. 367 (1988): applies the refusal to presume that jurors disregard an instruction's constitutionally defective route; no factor-specific verdict is invented.
- Walton v. Arizona, 497 U.S. 639 (1990): preserves genuine judicial sentencing and the presumption that judges apply legal narrowing; distinguishes a system in which a separate unguided recommendation carries required weight.
- Baldwin v. Alabama, 472 U.S. 372 (1985), and Spaziano v. Florida, 468 U.S. 447 (1984): preserve States' latitude in allocating sentencing responsibility; that latitude does not validate influential unguided weighing.
- Tedder v. State, 322 So.2d 908 (Fla. 1975), Smith v. State, 515 So.2d 182 (Fla. 1987), and Grossman v. State, 525 So.2d 833 (Fla. 1988): supply the state-law requirement to give great weight to jury recommendations of life or death.
- Smalley v. State, 546 So.2d 720 (Fla. 1989): rejects its premise that the jury's advisory designation alone makes this vague instruction constitutionally immaterial.

##### Correction must address the recommendation's influence on the death sentence

**Holding:** Reversal of the rejection of this sentencing claim requires further proceedings that remove the influence of the invalid jury recommendation through lawful reweighing or harmless-error review satisfying Chapman beyond a reasonable doubt. If no lawful cure is available, a new sentencing proceeding is required; valid remaining aggravators alone do not establish a cure, and neither an automatic life sentence nor disturbance of the guilt judgment follows.

**Proposition-level authority:** The per curiam opinion, joined by Stone, Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter and Thomas; seven Justices adopt the defect and corrective requirements. White favors argument and casts no present merits vote; Scalia dissents.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No automatic reduction to life, retrial of guilt, adjudication of unrelated aggravators, factor-by-factor jury finding, or collateral-review gateway rule follows. The petition's severance and mitigation/time/funding/proportionality questions are not granted or adjudicated in this limited summary action; no separate denial of them is invented. No prior Supreme Court decision is overruled.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Court grants limited review and reverses the rejection of the sentencing claim. Remand requires lawful reweighing or Chapman review addressing the recommendation's influence, and new sentencing if no lawful cure is available. Guilt and the ungranted severance and mitigation/time/funding/proportionality questions remain outside the disposition; no separate denial or automatic life sentence follows.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Clemons v. Mississippi, 494 U.S. 738 (1990): applies lawful appellate reweighing or harmless-error correction; merely counting valid aggravators does not cure the error.
- Chapman v. California, 386 U.S. 18 (1967): applies harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt; no lesser standard or burden on the defendant is created.
- Stringer v. Black, simulated March 9, 1992, and Sochor v. Florida, simulated June 8, 1992: apply actual cure requirements to the recommendation's transmitted influence; no unreasoned harmlessness label suffices.
- Parker v. Dugger, 498 U.S. 308 (1991): applies review grounded in the real sentencing record and mitigation, not an assumed alternative record.

### Capital sentencing and habeas retroactivity

#### Stringer v. Black, 503 U.S. 222 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 90-6616.
**Decided:** March 9, 1992.

##### Whether the Mississippi vague-aggravator claim seeks a new rule after February 19, 1985 finality

**Holding:** For a sentence final on February 19, 1985, Godfrey already prohibited the unguided heinousness aggravation later addressed in Maynard, and applying that protection to Mississippi’s weighing system does not create a new rule. Teague therefore does not bar consideration of this claim on the ground that Maynard or the corrective principles discussed in Clemons postdated finality.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens and O'Connor; six Justices adopt this proposition.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The holding is confined to the old-rule application established by Godfrey for this finality date. No Teague exception or unresolved procedural-default defense is decided.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Fifth Circuit’s Teague disposition is reversed and remanded for consideration of the preserved procedural-default defense and adequate state correction. If relief otherwise becomes warranted, a conditional writ may permit lawful resentencing or authorized appellate correction. No unconditional release, automatic life sentence, or finding that a particular state cure failed is ordered.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Teague v. Lane, 489 U.S. 288 — applied, not replaced: the claim seeks an old rule at the relevant finality date.
- Butler v. McKellar, 494 U.S. 407 — applied: both novelty of the later rule and novelty of its application must be considered.
- Godfrey v. Georgia, 446 U.S. 420 — applied: meaningful guidance was already required for the heinousness aggravator.
- Maynard v. Cartwright, 486 U.S. 356 — treated as applying Godfrey’s old rule to equivalent language.
- Clemons v. Mississippi, 494 U.S. 738 — applied as identifying permissible correction, not a newly created protection in this setting.

##### What correction a constitutionally invalid aggravator requires in a capital weighing system

**Holding:** When a capital sentencer weighs a constitutionally invalid aggravating factor against mitigation, remaining valid aggravators do not by themselves cure the error. The state judicial system must supply genuine reweighing without the invalid factor, where authorized, or constitutional harmless-error review establishing that the invalid factor did not affect the sentence; the adequacy of any cure here remains for further proceedings.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's opinion of the Court, joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens and O'Connor; six Justices adopt this proposition.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Genuine authorized reweighing and constitutional harmlessness are distinct corrective routes. The latter places on the State the burden of proving harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt. Remaining valid aggravators or bare proportionality review alone do not cure the error; death eligibility is not automatically negated.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The Fifth Circuit’s Teague disposition is reversed and remanded for consideration of the preserved procedural-default defense and adequate state correction. If relief otherwise becomes warranted, a conditional writ may permit lawful resentencing or authorized appellate correction. No unconditional release, automatic life sentence, or finding that a particular state cure failed is ordered.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Zant v. Stephens, 462 U.S. 862 — distinguished: its nonweighing holding does not automatically cure a weighing-system error.
- Barclay v. Florida, 463 U.S. 939 — distinguished: its actual review and state-law invalidity do not justify uncorrected constitutional aggravation.
- Clemons v. Mississippi, 494 U.S. 738 — applied: genuine appellate reweighing or constitutional harmlessness can correct a weighing error.
- Chapman v. California, 386 U.S. 18 — applied to the harmless-error route: the State must establish harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt.
- Lowenfield v. Phelps, 484 U.S. 231 — distinguished: duplication in narrowing does not answer vague-factor weighting and cannot supply a prefinality reliance premise.

### Compelled medication and fair trial

#### Riggins v. Nevada, 504 U.S. 127 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 90-8466.
**Decided:** May 18, 1992.

##### What justification is required to continue antipsychotic medication over a pretrial detainee’s objection

**Holding:** Once a pretrial detainee objects to continued antipsychotic medication, the State must establish medical appropriateness and a need sufficient to override the protected refusal interest, considering reasonable less intrusive means. The unexplained order here supplies neither an essential justification nor findings about alternatives and cannot authorize the compelled treatment through trial.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's Part II, joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens and Souter: six of nine participating Justices adopt this rule and application.

**Material application:** Continued medication became involuntary after objection. Medical appropriateness was accepted, but the unexplained order established neither essential safety need nor the insufficiency of less intrusive means; testimony indicated that competence might continue without Mellaril.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No incompetency finding, fixed treatment instruction, categorical medication prohibition, universal proof quantum, strict-scrutiny formula or rule making every medication error structural is adopted. The complete conditions for competency-restoration medication, competency waiver, the Fifth Amendment demeanor theory and an unpreserved Eighth Amendment theory remain undecided. Chapman’s harmless-beyond-a-reasonable-doubt formulation appears only in Stone’s concurrence.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The murder and robbery convictions and dependent death sentence are reversed and vacated, 7–2; the case is remanded for a new trial if the State proceeds. Renewed compelled treatment requires constitutionally adequate contemporaneous justification.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Washington v. Harper, 494 U.S. 210 (1990): applied for the protected refusal interest and requirement of overriding justification and medical appropriateness; its convicted-prisoner procedures do not automatically govern trial medication.
- Illinois v. Allen, 397 U.S. 337 (1970): relied on for the State's legitimate trial interest and the possibility of necessary courtroom measures; no comprehensive competency-medication exception is adopted.

##### Whether the unsupported treatment and unreconstructable trial risk require a new trial

**Holding:** When unjustified compelled antipsychotic medication through trial creates a supported, substantial risk of impairing the defense that the record cannot reliably reconstruct, the defendant need not demonstrate exactly how an unmedicated trial would have differed. The risk here extends beyond visible demeanor to testimony, comprehension and communication with counsel; explanatory expert testimony does not cure it, and the convictions and dependent sentence must be vacated for a new trial.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's Part III, joined by Stone, White, Blackmun, Stevens and Souter: six of nine participating Justices adopt this record-specific rule and remedy. Kennedy concurs in the reversal and new-trial judgment on a distinct trial-integrity ground.

**Material application:** The supported risk concerned attention, testimony, comprehension and communication with counsel as well as demeanor. Expert explanation cannot restore an altered conversation or response, and an unmedicated trial cannot reliably be reconstructed.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No incompetency finding, fixed treatment instruction, categorical medication prohibition, universal proof quantum, strict-scrutiny formula or rule making every medication error structural is adopted. The complete conditions for competency-restoration medication, competency waiver, the Fifth Amendment demeanor theory and an unpreserved Eighth Amendment theory remain undecided. Chapman’s harmless-beyond-a-reasonable-doubt formulation appears only in Stone’s concurrence.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The murder and robbery convictions and dependent death sentence are reversed and vacated, 7–2; the case is remanded for a new trial if the State proceeds. Renewed compelled treatment requires constitutionally adequate contemporaneous justification.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- Illinois v. Allen, 397 U.S. 337 (1970): applied by analogy to potentially prejudicial compelled trial measures and the need for an essential justification.
- Estelle v. Williams, 425 U.S. 501 (1976): applied by analogy to effects of compelled trial appearance that cannot be fully reconstructed from a transcript; its particular waiver disposition is not extended.

### Competency hearings

#### Medina v. California, 505 U.S. 437 (1992)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 90-8370.
**Decided:** June 22, 1992.

##### Whether California may assign the defendant the preponderance burden at a competency hearing

**Holding:** Due process permits California to require a defendant asserting incompetence to prove it by a preponderance at an adequate competency hearing with counsel and access to psychiatric evidence. This allocation determines the outcome when evidence is evenly balanced; it neither authorizes trial of a defendant established to be incompetent nor excuses a hearing when constitutionally sufficient doubt arises.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy, White, Scalia and Thomas expressly adopt this proposition in the principal opinion; O'Connor and Souter expressly adopt the same California-specific burden and adequacy conclusion in O'Connor's concurrence in the judgment. Six support the exact operative proposition, although no whole opinion has five joins. The methods are not logical subsets yielding a broader Marks rule; the categorical exclusion of Mathews from criminal procedure has only four supporters and does not control.

**Current force:** Remains controlling at the stated California preponderance-burden and adequate-hearing scope; no exclusive criminal due-process method controls.

**Material application:** The full hearing, counsel and psychiatric evidence supply constitutionally adequate protection despite the risk that incapacity may impair the defendant's ability to help prove it. No finding establishes actual incompetence or equipoise in Medina's hearing.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Dusky's competence definition, the duty to inquire, the prohibition on trial while incompetent and the prosecution's burden on offense elements remain unchanged. No higher proof quantum, insanity allocation, harmlessness of an invalid burden, retrospective feasibility or other trial error is decided.
